prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of the time-reversal-invariant Z2 topological insulator and the quantum spin Hall effect, and for the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe quantum wells.

statement.case_for: I keep B004 as my final position and my preferred configuration is unchanged from round 1. After the full exchange the scientific case looks stronger to me, not weaker, because no member disputes the physics: the chair's summary records that none argues against its standing, and that interpretive stability (about two decades of transport and ARPES confirmation) is accepted. Kane and Mele showed that time-reversal symmetry and spin-orbit coupling alone give a Z2 invariant and protected helical edge states with no applied field, and Molenkamp's group observed the predicted edge conduction in HgTe wells. It is a sharp prediction, falsifiable, then verified, and the invariant is computable, which is why it redirected materials search. I would give this citation in the narrow two-dimensional form above. That wording answers the chair's question directly: it claims neither the three-dimensional generalisation nor the HgTe design proposal, and it names what the three credited people did. Four members now prefer B004 with identical laureates, and I treat that as a convergence of independent scientific judgements, not as a reason in itself.
statement.case_against: The Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang omission remains a real defect. Their proposal identified HgTe as the platform and made Molenkamp's experiment possible, Zhang is deceased, and the cap of three leaves no seat for the proposers without removing one of the credited three. I cannot call that resolved, only bounded: the Z2 prediction and the first observation of the state are what the citation credits, and the HgTe proposal is the route to that observation. Seven of eight round-1 files raise this point, so it should be stated openly in the record. The second reservation is overlap with the 2016 prize. I still judge the physics distinct, because there the topology concerned quantised Hall conductance and phase transitions in the presence of a field, and here a symmetry-protected classification without one. But it is a fair reason for a member to prefer a different subfield this year.

responses.point: Mehlig prefers B009 and argues that waiting for the pairing mechanism may mean waiting indefinitely, so the mechanism should be treated as a question about a derived phase and not about the discovery.
responses.response: This is the strongest argument for B009 and I take it seriously. The prediction of flat bands at a magic angle and the observation of correlated and superconducting states can indeed be cited without naming a mechanism. My remaining concern is narrower than the mechanism: the experimental credit rests on Jarillo-Herrero alone, with Cao and the other 2018 co-authors outside the names, and the decisive experiments are seven to eight years old. B004 has no comparable gap on maturity. I do not move to B009 as my first choice, but I keep it as my first alternative, and if B004 founders on credit I would back B009 with a citation framed on the flat-band physics.

responses.point: Lindroth supports B006 as the only candidate that is mature, cleanly attributed and reproduced, and holds that the magic-wavelength lattice is a different physical idea from the comb and the ion-clock lineage.
responses.response: I accept the distinction. The magic-wavelength condition is a new concept, and I agree the comb is a tool the clock uses and does not overlap in credit. This moves me on one point: I no longer count the 2005 and 2012 prizes as a serious objection to B006. What I weigh differently is the clean-attribution argument. B006 is clean for the names given, but several national laboratories reproduced the result, and Lindroth herself notes that ion-clock groups may feel left out. B004 has a more serious gap, but the gap is a named proposal with a definite role, whereas the B006 boundary is diffuse. I rank B006 as a close second and my first alternative.

responses.point: Kroll ranks B006 first as a bounded, nameable achievement with already physical consequences, and asks whether the committee should see lattice clocks as a new concept or as precision within a lineage.
responses.response: I agree it is bounded and nameable, and your reply to me about citation wording is right: anchored in the lattice concept and its development to 10^-18, it claims neither the comb nor the ion lineages. Where I still differ is on the weight of conceptual novelty against metrological reach. For a discovery prize I put a new organising principle in quantum matter slightly above a precision step, even a concept-driven one. I also note that the pending redefinition of the second makes the practical payoff prospective, and I would not treat that as decisive for or against. Your Hall-laboratory disclosure seems fairly flagged to me; I would leave recusal to the committee, but I would not exclude your technical argument.

responses.point: Pearce, the chair, moved from B002 to B004 after the opening and asks that the BHZ omission be stated openly, while recording a possible bias toward B043.
responses.response: I welcome that move and I agree the omission must be written into the record, not smoothed over. I think the clean way to do that is the narrow citation: it ties the credit to the Z2 prediction and the first observation, so the committee can say plainly that the HgTe proposal and the 3D work were left outside it. On the Higgs, I still do not see a principled way to choose between founders and spokespersons among four names for three seats, so I would set B002 aside this year. That is an attribution judgement, not a doubt about the physics.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept the narrow Kane-Mele-Molenkamp citation without Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, or treat the omission as disqualifying; this is the one question that could change my choice.
Whether the 2016 overlap weighs more heavily with colleagues who prefer a different subfield than I have judged; I regard the physics as distinct but this is a judgement.
Whether the experimental credit for B009 can be defended with Jarillo-Herrero alone, and whether the pairing mechanism will clarify enough to make B009 stronger next year.
I recall the details of the HgTe and ARPES history from memory and have not checked priority dates against the supplied evidence.
statement.conflict_note: My earlier disclosure stands. I direct WACQT at Chalmers and collaborate with Delsing, Wilson and Kockum, and Chalmers hosted researchers associated with the 2025 prize, so I would recuse myself from deliberating on B015 (circuit QED). I have no documented connection to Kane, Mele, Molenkamp or the other credited names in B004, B006 or B009, and the round-1 exchange has not changed that.
